Identify deconvoluted spectra using retention indices and spectral libraries

Source: R/library_search.R
library_search.Rd

Search acquired nominal-mass bins with fast native spectral comparisons and column-specific retention-index filtering. Fitted ion totals are preserved.

Usage

library_search(
  x,
  library,
  calibration = NULL,
  ri = NULL,
  phase = c("DB5", "DB1", "DBWAX"),
  ri_tolerance = 30,
  n_matches = 5L,
  method = "stein_scott",
  pseudocount = NULL,
  extrapolate = FALSE,
  unknown_phase = NULL,
  ncores = NULL,
  batch_size = 4096L
)

# S3 method for class 'GCMSmatches'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'GCMSmatches'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A GCMSdeco fit, or a compound-by-mass matrix with numeric mass names.

library

A GCMSlibrary returned by read_msp(), read_gcms_id() or open_library().

calibration

RIcalibration from calibrate_ri(). For GCMSdeco fits, the stored alkane standard is used automatically when available.

ri

Optional RI vector, one value per query; overrides profile-based timing.

phase

RI column class: DB1 (nonpolar), DB5 (semi-standard nonpolar), or DBWAX (polar).

ri_tolerance

Maximum absolute RI difference, default 30. Inf requests an unconstrained spectral comparison, also allowing references without RI.

n_matches

Maximum number of matches per spectrum and scoring method.

method

One or more of stein_scott, cosine, hellinger, jensen_shannon, multinomial, or all. The default is the Stein–Scott weighted dot product.

pseudocount

Optional total for each query (or one common total), useful when passing L1-normalized spectra. GCMSdeco already retains fitted ion totals.

extrapolate

Allow linear RI extrapolation beyond the calibrated anchors.

unknown_phase

Optional explicit column-class assignment for library RI records whose phase is unknown. NULL excludes these from constrained searches.

ncores

Native search threads; NULL uses the physical core count.

batch_size

Maximum library spectra loaded per batch; bounds SQLite memory.

row.names, optional

Additional data-frame arguments.

...

Additional method arguments.

Value

A GCMSmatches list with matches (ranked long table), queries (including unassigned spectra), calibration, search settings and elapsed seconds. as.data.frame() extracts the match table. Matches are tentative annotations.

Details

RI filtering precedes spectral scoring. Only the chosen phase class is accepted within ri_tolerance; missing query RI produces no constrained matches. Multiple library RI measurements are compared using the closest. A compound with fewer eligible references returns fewer than n_matches. The same onset-plus-half-narrow-width coordinate is used for standards and fitted profiles. Unknown library column classes require an explicit assignment.

Let a and b be the acquired-bin intensities, N=sum(a), M=sum(b), p=a/N and q=b/M. stein_scott is the squared cosine between a^0.6 * mass^3 and b^0.6 * mass^3; cosine uses unweighted intensities. hellinger uses sqrt(1-sum(sqrt(p*q))). jensen_shannon uses sqrt((KL(p,r)+KL(q,r))/(2*log(2))) with r=(p+q)/2. multinomial returns the symmetric two-sample deviance 2*(N*KL(p,u)+M*KL(q,u)), u=(a+b)/(N+M), retaining both totals. Zero contributions use 0*log(0)=0. These distances are finite with disjoint support.

Scores run from 0 to 1000, with 1000 denoting identical spectral shape: squared cosine, Bhattacharyya coefficient, 1-normalized-JS, and 1/(1+deviance), respectively. Compare scores within a method. The returned distance is the quantity minimized in ranking. Relative library intensities are pseudocounts; their arbitrary scale affects multinomial deviance. An explicit library Pseudocount/Ion_total tag supplies the original total when available. Hellinger and equal-weight Jensen–Shannon compare shapes independently of that scale. query_total, library_total and library_mass_coverage make the count and acquisition conventions explicit.

References are restricted to mass bins actually acquired for the query. Spectra are streamed from SQLite in bounded batches. Native OpenMP workers compare queries independently with deterministic ranking and no nested fitting.

References

Stein, S. E. and Scott, D. R. (1994). J. Am. Soc. Mass Spectrom. 5, 859–866. doi:10.1016/1044-0305(94)87009-8. Kim, S. et al. (2012). Bioinformatics 28, 1158–1163. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bts083.

Examples

f <- tempfile(fileext=".msp")
writeLines(c("Name: compound A", "RI_DB5: 1000", "Num Peaks: 3",
             "43 100; 57 80; 71 20;", "Name: compound B", "RI_DB5: 1200",
             "Num Peaks: 2", "43 20; 91 100;"), f)
lib <- read_msp(f)
q <- matrix(c(500,400,100,0),1,dimnames=list(NULL,c(43,57,71,91)))
hit <- library_search(q,lib,ri=1005,phase="DB5",method="all",ncores=1)
as.data.frame(hit)
